title: White chicken chilli
subtitle: Creamy American chicken-and-white-bean chilli
excerpt: Shredded poached chicken and white beans in a creamy cumin-and-green-chilli broth, topped with sour cream, avocado, and lime. A lighter, crowd-pleasing American chilli that emerged in the American Southwest in the 1980s.
sourceNotes: White chicken chilli emerged in American Southwest cooking in the 1980s, first appearing in the Hatch Valley of New Mexico and popularised nationally through food magazines and community cookbooks during the 1990s. It is a creamy variation on the older tradition of white chilli (stew of white beans and pork or chicken without tomatoes or red chillies), documented in Southwestern American cooking texts. The cream cheese version became widely distributed in American food media in the 1990s and 2000s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the cream cheese. Defrost, reheat gently, then stir in the cream cheese.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently and stir in the cream cheese at the end.

content.text: White chicken chilli is the milder, creamier cousin of red chilli, and it is one of the fastest crowd-feeding dishes in American cooking. Shredded chicken, white beans, a can of green chillies, cumin, and a brick of cream cheese stirred in at the end: that is the whole recipe. It takes under an hour from start to finish and people always want more of it.

items.prepNote: chopped; or use 2 fresh Anaheim/Hatch chillies, roasted and peeled
for mild heat; omit for no heat at all

content.text: Place the chicken breasts in the saucepan with the stock. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 18 to 20 minutes until cooked through. Lift out and shred with two forks. Reserve the poaching stock.
Heat the oil in the same pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute. Add the green chillies and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, reserved stock, and shredded chicken. Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pan to thicken the broth. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cream cheese in pieces, stirring until completely melted and smooth. Taste and season. Serve with sour cream, diced avocado, lime wedges, and tortilla chips or warm tortillas.

items.cause: Beans not mashed enough to release starch
items.fix: Use a potato masher to mash about a third of the beans in the pot. Or blend 200 ml of the chilli with the cream cheese and stir back in.

content.text: White chicken chilli is a dish of the American Southwest. It spread through the broader American food culture of the 1990s, appearing in food magazines, community cookbooks, and church supper menus across the country. It is associated with New Mexico Hatch chilli culture. Anaheim and New Mexican varieties provide the green chilli base. In most American kitchens it is made with tinned green chillies, which are entirely authentic for a dish that was never pretentious to begin with.
